tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: List Customer.io automations (campaigns) in the workspace, with their trigger type and state

tools.name: list_newsletters
tools.description: List Customer.io newsletters (one-time sends), most recent first when sorted desc

limit.description: Max newsletters to return per page (default 20, max 100)

sort.description: Optional sort order, asc for chronological or desc for reverse chronological

start.description: Optional pagination token from a previous response's next property

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: List Customer.io segments with their type, state and description

tools.name: get_customer_activities
tools.description: List recent Customer.io activities for one person (message sends, attribute changes, events) from the last 30 days

customer_id.description: The identifier of the person to look up (by default their id)

id_type.description: Which identifier customer_id is, defaults to id

type.description: Optional activity type to filter by (e.g. sent_email, opened_email, attribute_change, event)

limit.description: Max activities to return per page (default 20, max 100)

needs_review: Scaffolded auth was WRONG for these tools and was fixed. The scaffold had base_url https://track.customer.io with basic auth (site_id + api_key) and test GET /auth, which is the Track (ingress) API. Campaigns, newsletters, segments and activities are App API reads, and the official App API spec (https://docs.customer.io/files/journeys-app.json) declares servers https://api.customer.io (US) and https://api-eu.customer.io (EU) with security scheme Bearer-Auth, an App API Key. The integration type registry already labels the api_key field 'App API Key', so the bearer key is what a user supplies. base_url is now https://api.customer.io and auth is bearer on api_key.

site_id stays in requiredFields because the credential type in src/config/integrationTypes.js marks it required and the Track API pairing needs it, but no App API tool reads it. A workspace in the EU region answers on https://api-eu.customer.io only, and the spec has no per-credential base_url override, so EU customers would need that variant: flagged rather than silently guessed.

test was moved from GET /auth (Track API) to GET /v1/segments: the App API publishes no dedicated credential-check route, so the cheapest documented read doubles as the connection test. A key scoped narrowly enough to exclude segment reads will fail the test while other tools still work.

list_campaigns and list_segments take no documented query parameters, so both carry an empty input schema rather than invented paging. get_customer_activities uses GET /v1/activities with a customer_id query parameter rather than /v1/customers/{customer_id}/activities, so it needs no path identifier and no _probe hint.
